decisions.label: documented-and-verifiable
decisions.evidence_note: eval_baseline.py and eval_private.py show that HumanEval problems are read via read_problems() and predictions are written as JSONL with fields {task_id, completion}; README shows evaluate_functional_correctness consuming the resulting *.samples.jsonl file.

decisions.label: partially-documented
decisions.evidence_note: README specifies the command evaluate_functional_correctness <samples_path> and reports Pass@1/10/100, but it does not define how pass@k is computed; details are delegated to the external human-eval repository, not included here.

decisions.label: claimed-but-not-verifiable
decisions.evidence_note: Core evaluation is delegated to the external human-eval package (install and use evaluate_functional_correctness). Only sample-generation code is present; the actual evaluator implementation is not included in this packet.

decisions.label: not-documented
decisions.evidence_note: There is no description of how individual test outcomes are turned into scores, how multiple samples per task are handled, or any tie-breaking/rounding rules. Only metric names and an external evaluation command are mentioned.

decisions.label: not-documented
decisions.evidence_note: Code shows how to generate per-task samples.jsonl files but not how these are converted into aggregate Pass@k scores; this logic resides in evaluate_functional_correctness in the external human-eval repo, which is not shown here.

decisions.label: not-documented
decisions.evidence_note: Scripts describe how to generate *.samples.jsonl and the README shows the expected filename, but no actual prediction or trajectory files are included in the packet.
